# Battle of Scerdilaidas

Battle of Scerdilaidas was a military engagement fought in the early 3rd century BCE between the forces of the Illyrian king Scerdilaidas and the Greek Aetolian League. The battle took place along the Adriatic coast in the region inhabited by the Illyrians, although the precise location remains uncertain. It resulted in a decisive Illyrian victory that reinforced Illyrian dominance in the region.
Background
The Illyrians were a group of tribes inhabiting the western Balkans and the eastern Adriatic coast. Under the reign of King Scerdilaidas (c. 230–210 BCE), the Illyrians expanded their influence both militarily and politically, particularly challenging Greek powers such as the Aetolian League. Scerdilaidas was known for his naval prowess and military skill, which enabled him to secure territories and control important trade routes along the Adriatic Sea.
The Aetolian League, a confederation of Greek city-states in central Greece, had frequently been involved in conflicts with neighboring powers to expand or maintain its influence. Tensions with Illyrian tribes often escalated into open warfare as both sides vied for control of coastal cities and maritime dominance.
The battle
Although the precise details of the battle are scarce, historical reconstructions based on ancient sources suggest that Scerdilaidas personally led his forces against an Aetolian coalition along the Adriatic coast. The Illyrians leveraged their familiarity with the rugged coastal terrain and their superior naval capabilities. The Aetolian forces suffered heavy casualties, and their defeat curtailed their ambitions in the region for a time.
Aftermath
The victory at the Battle of Scerdilaidas solidified Illyrian control over parts of the Adriatic coast and bolstered King Scerdilaidas’s reputation as a formidable leader. However, despite this success, Illyrian power eventually waned with the rising influence of Rome and Macedon later in the 3rd century BCE.
